meta.basis: Six cross-cutting forces from the Sectors research, split into investable origin themes. Candidates are drawn from the unresearched bench of the merged dip+pro queue (502 names), 10 per theme, each assigned one primary theme.

candidates.fit: Largest defense prime; missile/air-defense demand is the direct geopolitics beneficiary
B-21, Sentinel and space/missile-defense backlog levered to deterrence spending
Submarines, combat vehicles and munitions restocking
Largest US refiner; refining margins widen when crude supply is disrupted
Crude tanker owner; tonne-mile demand and day rates spike on route disruption
Western uranium champion; nuclear energy security and enrichment decoupling from Russia
Only scaled US rare-earth producer; China export controls are its demand story
Copper giant; critical-mineral security plus electrification demand
Gold miner; geopolitical hedge demand with gold near record territory
Gold royalty model — hedge exposure without mine-operating risk

themes.name: Geopolitics & Energy Security
themes.thesis: The Iran-war oil shock (Brent +85% YTD, diesel +67% y/y) and great-power supply-chain rivalry are repricing energy security, defense and critical minerals. Origin thesis: companies the shock pays — refiners, tanker owners, uranium and rare-earth suppliers, defense primes — rather than companies it taxes.
themes.watch: Ceasefire or escalation headlines, OPEC spare capacity, defense appropriations into the midterms, China export controls on rare earths and gallium.

candidates.fit: Insurer with pricing power; investment income compounds at 5% rates
Archetypal pricing-power staple; has taken price through every inflation wave
Pricing-power consumer franchise with premium mix shift
Rates-volatility exchange; hedging volumes rise when the rate path is contested
Largest NIM and markets beneficiary of higher-for-longer
Membership pricing power; inflation drives trade-in traffic
Trade-down winner; grocery share gains when budgets squeeze
Low-cost gold producer; real-asset hedge with operating leverage
Insurer float income repricing upward; disciplined underwriting
Data/index monopoly with contractual price escalators

themes.name: Inflation & Rates
themes.thesis: September CPI 3.7% y/y, PPI 6.3%, a Fed that hiked in September and a 10-year at 5.00% say inflation is sticky, not beaten. Origin thesis: pricing-power franchises that pass costs through, and financials whose earnings rise with rates — float income, NIM, rate-volatility volumes.
themes.watch: Oct 28 FOMC, Dec hike pricing, core PCE trend, whether the 10-year holds above or breaks below 5%.

Exchange and index licensing leveraged to capital-markets activity
Asset-gathering toll on rising markets and private-credit growth
Cheap global bank bellwether; restructuring plus buybacks into a growing economy
Parcel bellwether for US/world trade volumes
Eastern rail bellwether for industrial and consumer freight
Best-in-class LTL carrier; freight-cycle leverage with pricing discipline
Housing-adjacent retail bellwether; pro segment growth
Auto-cycle bellwether with ICE profit engine funding buybacks
Trading-activity toll-taker; accounts and volumes compound through cycles

themes.name: Economics & Growth
themes.thesis: Flash composite PMI 57.6 says the real economy is still expanding even as payrolls cool — a strong-but-pricey economy. Origin thesis: bellwethers and toll-takers whose volumes read the cycle directly — exchanges, payments of market activity, freight, housing-adjacent retail.
themes.watch: GDP/PCE prints, PMI new orders, freight volumes, housing starts as mortgage rates sit at 7.40%.

Payroll/HR software for mid-market employers; seat growth tracks hiring
Uniform and workplace services rented per employee; route density moat
Route-based services (Orkin); labor-light recurring model
Workplace food/facility services directly tied to return-to-office employment
Factory automation — the capex answer to scarce, expensive labor
Robotics (UR) plus chip-test automation; labor-substitution demand
Warehouse and industrial automation portfolio
MRO distribution into every workplace; same-day labor-saving logistics
Onsite vending/industrial supply embedded at customer plants

themes.name: Employment & Labor
themes.thesis: Payrolls printed +29k vs ~85k expected and unemployment is 4.2% — labor is cooling but scarce skills stay expensive. Origin thesis: the payroll/HR infrastructure every employer must keep, plus the automation vendors employers buy when hiring gets hard.
themes.watch: Monthly payrolls and revisions, JOLTS, wage growth, staffing-agency commentary.

themes.name: Innovation
themes.thesis: AI capital spending in the hundreds of billions, surgical robotics, RNA medicines and chip-IP licensing are compounding on technology curves, not the business cycle. Origin thesis: platform innovators a dip screen misses (not dipped) and a factor screen under-rates (story precedes the revisions).
themes.watch: Hyperscaler capex guides, AI product revenue conversion, FDA/Phase 3 readouts, foundry capex plans.

themes.name: Politics & Policy
themes.thesis: 50% tariffs on ~$20B of Canadian goods, Section 232/338 actions, an $8B farm fuel-relief package and the Nov 3 midterms (Dem House ~0.915 on prediction markets) make policy a first-order price factor. Origin thesis: tariff-protected domestic producers, policy-funded sectors, and names whose regulatory weather is turning favorable.
themes.watch: Tariff proclamations and exemptions (Oct 30 wave), midterm results, CMS reimbursement rules, farm-bill and relief votes.
